findings.title: Arbitrary Origin is reflected WITH credentials
findings.description: The server echoes whatever Origin it receives into Access-Control-Allow-Origin and allows credentials, so any website can make authenticated requests as the victim and read the responses.
findings.evidence: Origin: https://evil-attacker.example -> Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://evil-attacker.example; Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true
findings.remediation: Validate Origin against an exact allow-list of trusted origins and only then echo it; never combine reflection with Allow-Credentials.

findings.title: CSP allows 'unsafe-inline' scripts
findings.description: Inline <script> and event handlers are allowed, which defeats most of CSP's XSS protection.
findings.remediation: Remove 'unsafe-inline'; use nonces or hashes instead.

findings.title: CSP allows scripts from overly broad sources
findings.description: Scheme-wide or wildcard script sources let an attacker load code from any host.
findings.remediation: List explicit trusted hosts or use nonces with 'strict-dynamic'.

findings.title: No clickjacking protection
findings.description: Neither X-Frame-Options nor CSP frame-ancestors is set, so the page can be framed by any site (UI redressing / clickjacking).
findings.evidence: X-Frame-Options and CSP frame-ancestors not present.
findings.remediation: Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none'  (or 'self'); add X-Frame-Options: DENY for legacy browsers.

findings.title: Referrer-Policy leaks full URLs
findings.description: unsafe-url sends the full URL (path and query) to every destination, including over HTTP.

findings.title: Cookie 'sessionid' missing HttpOnly flag
findings.description: JavaScript can read the cookie, so any XSS can steal it.

findings.title: State-changing methods allowed cross-origin to an untrusted origin
findings.description: The preflight response approves methods that change server state for an origin that should not be trusted.
findings.remediation: Allow only the methods the trusted front-end needs, and only for trusted origins.

findings.title: CSP allows 'unsafe-eval'
findings.description: eval()/Function() style code execution is permitted.
findings.remediation: Remove 'unsafe-eval' and refactor code that needs it.

findings.title: CSP does not lock down object-src
findings.description: Plugins (<object>/<embed>) are not restricted to 'none'.

findings.title: CSP does not restrict base-uri
findings.description: An injected <base> tag could redirect relative URLs; base-uri is not covered by default-src.

findings.title: X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff missing
findings.description: Browsers may MIME-sniff responses and execute content as a different type.
findings.evidence: Header not present in the response.

findings.title: Permissions-Policy missing
findings.description: Powerful browser features (camera, microphone, geolocation...) are not explicitly restricted.
findings.evidence: Header not present in the response.

findings.title: Server header discloses a version
findings.description: Version banners help attackers pick exploits for known vulnerabilities.
findings.remediation: Strip the version (e.g. nginx: server_tokens off; Apache: ServerTokens Prod).

findings.title: X-Powered-By header discloses technology
findings.description: Framework/runtime banners reveal the technology stack.
findings.remediation: Remove the X-Powered-By header in the framework or reverse-proxy configuration.

findings.title: Cookie 'sessionid' has no SameSite attribute
findings.description: Behaviour then depends on the browser default; explicit SameSite helps against CSRF.

findings.title: Cookie 'theme' missing HttpOnly flag
findings.description: JavaScript can read the cookie, so any XSS can steal it.

findings.title: Cookie 'theme' has no SameSite attribute
findings.description: Behaviour then depends on the browser default; explicit SameSite helps against CSRF.

findings.title: Dynamic CORS response lacks Vary: Origin
findings.description: Shared caches may serve one origin's CORS headers to another origin (cache poisoning or intermittent breakage).
findings.remediation: Add 'Vary: Origin' whenever Access-Control-Allow-Origin depends on the request.

findings.title: Preflight allows arbitrary request headers
findings.description: A wildcard or echoed Allow-Headers lets untrusted origins send any custom header, e.g. Authorization.

findings.title: HTTPS checks skipped for loopback target
findings.description: HSTS, Secure-cookie and HTTP->HTTPS checks are not meaningful on localhost.

findings.title: Cross-origin isolation headers not set
findings.description: COOP/COEP/CORP mitigate cross-origin leaks (Spectre-style) and window handle abuse. They are recommended hardening rather than a vulnerability.

findings.title: Legacy X-XSS-Protection filter enabled
findings.description: The old XSS auditor is removed from modern browsers and could itself introduce side-channel issues in older ones.
findings.remediation: Send X-XSS-Protection: 0 (or omit) and rely on a strict CSP.

findings.title: Very long preflight cache time
findings.description: Policy changes take a long time to take effect (browsers cap the value anyway).

findings.title: Origin 'null' is trusted with credentials
findings.description: Sandboxed iframes, data: URLs and local files send Origin: null, so an attacker can trigger requests that the server will accept.
findings.evidence: Origin: null -> Access-Control-Allow-Origin: null; Allow-Credentials: true
findings.remediation: Never allow 'null' in the origin allow-list.

findings.title: Origin validation can be bypassed (credentials allowed)
findings.description: Look-alike origins that merely start or end with the real hostname are accepted, which indicates substring/prefix/suffix matching instead of exact comparison.
findings.remediation: Compare the full, parsed origin against an exact allow-list; avoid startswith/endswith/regex shortcuts.

findings.title: Cookie 'sid' uses SameSite=None without Secure
findings.description: Browsers reject SameSite=None cookies that are not Secure, and it exposes the cookie to cross-site requests.
findings.evidence: Cookie 'sid' (value redacted); attributes: httponly, path, samesite

findings.title: HTTPS checks skipped for loopback target
findings.description: HSTS, Secure-cookie and HTTP->HTTPS checks are not meaningful on localhost.

findings.title: Content-Security-Policy missing
findings.description: CSP is the main defence-in-depth control against XSS and data injection.
findings.evidence: Header not present in the response.
findings.remediation: Start from: default-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'  and tighten per page.

findings.title: Referrer-Policy missing
findings.description: Without an explicit policy, referrer leakage depends on browser defaults.
findings.evidence: Header not present in the response.

findings.title: Permissions-Policy missing
findings.description: Powerful browser features (camera, microphone, geolocation...) are not explicitly restricted.
findings.evidence: Header not present in the response.

findings.title: Access-Control-Allow-Origin is a wildcard
findings.description: Any website can read responses from this URL. That is fine for fully public, unauthenticated data but wrong for anything user-specific.
findings.remediation: Replace * with an allow-list of origins unless the resource is intentionally public.
